points.why: It treats the board's objection as a structural challenge to the model's boundary and plans to win acceptance by building the loop with the board members and letting them name the pattern first.
It names driver capacity as outside the boundary, notes that crowding and unreliability would brake ridership gains, and says to check whether the forecast quietly assumes the full schedule runs.

It moves the union and operations to consulted before the meeting and asks them to check the loop, but the whiteboard co-building with the skeptical board members seems to happen at the meeting rather than before it.

It sensitivity-tests elasticity, share of new riders from cars, hiring rate and lag against the decision, but never frames counting congestion benefits or the three-year horizon as value-laden choices to name openly.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly changes who is consulted by bringing in the union, scheduling and HR before the board meeting.
